title: GMT: GPU Orchestrated Memory Tiering for the Big Data Era
problem: GPUs need to access storage systems (SSDs) for larger datasets, but existing mechanisms either use host CPUs as intermediaries (Dragon, HMM) which perform poorly and cannot meet GPU throughput needs, or directly access SSDs through NVMe (BaM) which forgo the lower latencies possible with host memory as an intermediate tier.
motivation: As the demand for processing larger datasets increases, GPUs require efficient access to storage capacity beyond their local memory hierarchy.
method: GMT implements a GPU-orchestrated 3-tier memory hierarchy comprising GPU memory, host memory, and SSDs, where the GPU orchestrates bandwidth/latency-sensitive transfers. The system employs a reuse-prediction based insertion policy to perform discretionary page placement and bypass, avoiding blind transfers of all pages to host memory upon eviction.
key_novelty: GPU-orchestrated memory tiering that places control at the GPU rather than the host CPU, enabling efficient multi-tier memory access.
contributions: Design and implementation of GPU-orchestrated 3-tier memory hierarchy (GPU memory, host memory, SSDs)
Reuse-prediction based insertion policy for smart page placement and bypass decisions
50% performance improvement over 2-tier strategies (BaM) and 350% improvement over 3-tier host-orchestrated strategies (HMM)

metrics.speedup: 50% better than BaM, 350% better than HMM
